chunks: Ali, from his father, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Zurara, who said:
Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'It suffices the woman for the wiping of the head that she wipes its front by the measure of three fingers, and she should not cast off her scarf from her.'
ai.seo_question: What is the minimum requirement for wiping the head during wudu according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the Shia jurisprudential view that wiping the front of the head is sufficient for wudu, distinguishing it from the Sunni practice of wiping the entire head. The condition that the woman must not remove her khimar highlights the continuity of her head covering during the ritual act, ensuring the wiped area remains part of the head's covered region. This ruling is foundational in al-Kafi for establishing the minimal valid area for masah in Shia fiqh.

en.hubeali: Ali, from his father, form Hammad, from Hareyz, from zurara who said,

‘Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The woman, it would suffice her from the wiping of the head that she wipes its front by a measurement of three fingers, and she should not cast off her scarf from her’.
en.sarwar: 5. Ali has narrated from his father from Hammad from Hariz from Zurarah who has said the following: “
Abu Ja’far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘In the case of women it is sufficient for them to wipe the front portion of their head the size of three fingers without removing their head scarf.’”
